pins.definition: The organ inside the body where food goes and is digested.
The organ inside the body where food goes and is digested after being eaten.
The front part of the body between the chest and the hips; the abdomen.

situation: A medical illustrator at a wooden desk lays out anatomical diagrams beside a physical model showing the digestive tract.
subject: the human stomach
brief: An engraved scientific plate displays a detailed anatomical view of the human torso, with the stomach clearly isolated, shaded in soft sepia tones, and labeled to show its distinct curved pouch shape between the esophagus and intestines.
prompt: An engraved scientific plate displays a detailed anatomical view of the human torso, with the stomach clearly isolated, shaded in soft sepia tones, and labeled to show its distinct curved pouch shape between the esophagus and intestines. a nineteenth-century engraved scientific plate, fine hatching, hand-tinted washes, aged rag paper, the specimen isolated and reverently observed. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
